section_title: Why did Paul preach to the Corinthians free of charge?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 7 Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge? 8 I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you. 9 And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.
10 As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia. 11 Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!

context_lines: Paul turns to another point of criticism: his decision to preach the gospel to the Corinthians without charging them. He asks whether humbling himself so they could be lifted up was somehow a sin. The question exposes the unfairness of treating his service as a reason to dismiss him.

Other churches helped support that work. Paul describes accepting their support with the striking word robbed, emphasizing the cost they bore while Corinth benefited. He also says brothers from Macedonia supplied his needs when he was among the Corinthians.

His practice therefore included receiving support, while deliberately keeping from being a financial burden to Corinth. [Philippians 4:15–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/philippians/4.htm) offers another account of churches sharing in his ministry through gifts.

Paul intends to continue his approach in Achaia. He closes by answering a possible misunderstanding: his refusal to take their support does not mean he lacks love for them. God knows that he loves them.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read this as a defense of Paul’s decision to serve Corinth without taking support from them. [Wesley’s notes on verses 7–11](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) and the [USCCB notes on verses 7–12](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/2corinthians/11) both explain that decision within his response to criticism. His stated love and the support he received from elsewhere remain part of the picture.
